1 The petitioners seek to quash the final report in S.C.No.590 of 2025 on the file of the Sessions Court (Mahila Court), Madurai, which was filed for the offences under Sections 294(b), 417 and 376 of IPC.
2.

The allegation in the final report is that the petitioners and the defacto complainant had consensual relationship; that on the promise of marriage, the petitioner had sexual intercourse with the second respondent and thus, committed the aforesaid offences.
3. Admittedly, the petitioners and the second respondent have now entered into a compromise and decided to give a quietus to the entire dispute.

The parties have filed a joint compromise memo dated 6 th October 2025 and the scanned copy of the compromise memo reads as follows:

The second respondent/defacto complainant is present before this Court and she confirms the compromise and that she does not wish to prosecute the case further.

5. The petitioners, namely, Duraipandi (Aadhaar No.2626 4028 9593), Maheswari (Aadhaar No.5885 5470 6540) and the second respondent, namely, Alagu (Aadhaar No.9165 9561 0354) are present before this Court in person.

They are identified by Mr.R.Ramuthai, Women Head Constable,
Thirumangalam AWPS, Madurai District.
All the parties confirmed the compromise arrived at between them.

6. In view of the same and considering the nature of the offences and the relationship between the parties, this Court is of the view that no useful purpose would be served by keeping the proceedings pending trial.
Accordingly, the impugned final report in S.C.No.590 of 2025 on the file of the Sessions Court (Mahalir Neethimandram), Madurai, is quashed.
Further, it appears that the first petitioner is employed in a Government job.

Admittedly since there was a consensual relationship between the first petitioner and the second respondent and since the impugned proceedings have now been quashed, it is needless to say that no stigma shall be attached to the first petitioner.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
In the result, the Criminal Original Petition stands allowed.
